title: SDK client governance, escape hatches, and cross-language compatibility for pagination/retries/streaming
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Summary: Establish a cross-language governance layer and set of 'escape hatches' for Redwood SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) to ensure safe evolution of pagination, retries, and streaming APIs. This PRD clarifies requirements, scope changes requested by eng/design, migration patterns, and concrete acceptance criteria. Motivation: Multiple customers and platform teams have reported subtle incompatibilities and surprising behavior when clients upgrade across minor SDK versions or when server-side streaming semantics change. We need a reproducible conformance approach that balances strict contracts with pragmatic escape hatches for rapid incident mitigation.
objectives: Define a minimal compatibility contract for pagination cursors and offsets across Python/TS/Go clients
Standardize retry semantics and backoff configurations exposed by SDKs (retry budgets, idempotency markers)
Specify a resumable streaming handshake for server-client resumption and gap-detection
Provide documented escape hatches (raw HTTP, allowlist feature flags, opt-out headers) for on-call mitigation
Deliver a conformance test suite and CI gating for client releases
scope_inclusions: SDK surface changes (new flags, helper primitives) for pagination cursors and cursor metadata
New retry configuration primitives: RetryBudget, MaxAttempts, PerRoutePolicies, and default idempotency hints
Streaming resume handshake: ResumeToken semantics, server-side last-ack offsets, and client-side gap reconciliation
Migration guides and semver compatibility notes for each language
Conformance test harness and a runnable matrix (Python/TS/Go) linked in CI
scope_exclusions: Large runtime-level batching/kernel optimizations (handled by runtime team)
Backend-only cursor format changes that don't affect client surface (unless needed for interop)
Custom per-customer SDK forks (those customers will be serviced via Dedicated/Private contracts)
Changes to authentication primitives beyond standard headers and token passthrough
constraints_and_assumptions: All SDKs must maintain existing public method names where possible; new helpers should be additive
Cursor payloads must remain opaque to most clients; we will publish a stable envelope with version and metadata
Streaming protocol is over existing HTTP/2 and SSE/WS flavors; no new transport-level dependencies
We assume one quarterly coordinated release for SDKs to avoid fragmented versions during rollout
key_decisions: Adopt an explicit cursor envelope: {"v":"1","payload":"<opaque>","meta":{"server_ts":"..."}} (clients treat payload as opaque except for version) - published in docs
Define RetryBudget default to 10% of QPS with exponential jittered backoff and an application-level MaxAttempts override
Streaming resume will use a ResumeToken that encodes (shard_id, last_commit_offset, stream_version); server will return a resume-ack with earliest available offset
Provide 'raw_http' escape hatch in SDKs to send requests without client-side cursor manipulation (for urgent mitigation)
Compatibility testing will include interop runs where older client versions connect to newer server versions and vice versa
acceptance_criteria: API: SDKs expose new pagination helpers: CursorEnvelope parser, CursorVersion guard, and a high-level Pager that returns a resumable iterator
Retries: Default retry behavior conforms to RetryBudget policy; SDKs expose per-call override and idempotency hint parameter and pass idempotency to the server via x-rw-idempotency header
Streaming: Client and server perform the resume handshake; e2e tests demonstrate resumption after simulated disconnects with zero-duplicate semantics for at-least-once streams
Escape hatches: raw_http and 'disable_client_cursor_manipulation' flag available in all SDKs documented in the migration guide
Conformance: CI matrix runs (Python 3.10/3.11, Node 18/20, Go 1.20/1.21) pass all interop tests; failures block the SDK release pipeline
Docs: Migration guides and compatibility matrix published in docs.redwood.ai and linked from SDK changelog
Rollout: Canary release to 5% of hosted traffic with automatic rollback on >5% increase in 95th percentile latency or any customer-facing errors
Telemetry: SDKs emit a stable metric 'rw.sdk.client_version' and 'rw.sdk.cursor_version' for usage and regression detection
technical_requirements: Cursor envelope: a stable JSON wrapper with version integer; SDKs must validate envelope version and surface a clear error on unknown versions
Backoff: jittered exponential backoff implementation with configurable base and cap exposed in each SDK
migration_strategy: Phased: 1) Additive SDK helpers and feature flags (no breaking changes). 2) Opt-in early access: enable client-side cursor validation for a small cohort. 3) Publish migration guide and tooling to convert existing cursors if backend rotation required. 4) Deprecation: after two quarters, mark old behaviors as deprecated with clear removals in release notes.
deliverables: Language spec doc describing cursor envelope, resume token, retry headers
SDK patches implementing helpers and escape hatches (python-sdk PR, ts-sdk PR, go-sdk PR)
Conformance test harness + CI matrix jobs
Migration guide and code examples in docs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cursor envelope leaks implementation details causing tight coupling - Mitigation: enforce opaque payload and only expose version and metadata fields
Risk: Retry budget tuning causes latent request spikes - Mitigation: telemetry and canary with automated rollback thresholds
Risk: Streaming resume introduces duplication semantics - Mitigation: at-least-once with idempotency markers and server-side dedupe where feasible
notes: Engineering requested an explicit 'escape hatch' primitive after incident RW-INC-2024-11 where client-side cursor handling prevented emergency hotfix. Design asked for example UX patterns in Python and TS to avoid surprising ergonomics. Security reviewed header additions; no KMS changes required. Eng also proposed an alternate lightweight binary resume token but decided to defer until we complete the JSON envelope pilot.

qa_plan: Conformance tests: unit + integration + chaos tests (simulate network flaps). Interop matrix: run all permutations of client versions {v_old,v_new} against server versions {v_old,v_new}. Post-release: monitor 'rw.sdk.client_version' for adoption and 'rw.sdk.cursor_errors' for regression spikes.
release_notes_summary: Additive SDK changes to support a stable cursor envelope, explicit retry budget primitives, streaming resume handshake, and emergency escape hatches. Backwards-compatible by default with opt-in strict validation.
open_questions: Should resume tokens be encrypted for multi-tenant deployments? (security asked for risk assessment)
What is the exact timeline for deprecating legacy cursor behaviors given enterprise upgrade cycles?
Do we standardize RetryBudget units as percentage-of-qps or absolute token counts?
